paragraphs: On Thursday, Teacher Kim brought a box of cards to the library. "Today we play the Big and Small Quiz," she said. "I read a card, and you say which one is bigger, faster, or heavier." Mia and Leo were one team, and Lily and May were the other team. Each team got one point for a good answer.

"Card one," said Teacher Kim. "Which is heavier, a wild tiger or a wild elephant?" "An elephant is heavier than a tiger," said Leo. "But a tiger is faster," said Mia. "That is right," said Teacher Kim. "One point for Mia and Leo." "Card two. Which is hotter in the day, a desert or a forest?" "A desert is hotter than a forest," said Lily. "And a forest has more water," said May. "One point for Lily and May," said Teacher Kim.

"Card three. Which is smaller, a violin or a guitar?" "A violin is smaller than a guitar," said Mia. "It is also not as heavy as a guitar," said Leo. "Two points for Mia and Leo!" said Teacher Kim. "Card four. Is a violin louder than a drum?" Lily thought for a minute. "No, a drum is louder," she said. "Good, Lily," said Teacher Kim. "The teams have two points each."

"Card five," said Teacher Kim. "On a long road, which is faster, a bus or a bicycle?" "A bus is faster than a bicycle," said Leo. "A bicycle is not as fast as a bus, is it?" asked Leo. May laughed. "That was a hard card, but Leo is right," she said. "Three points for Mia and Leo," said Teacher Kim. "Card six. Which is taller, a giraffe or an elephant?" "A giraffe is taller than an elephant," said May. "Three points for Lily and May," said Teacher Kim. "Now it is time to stop."

"We have three points each," said Teacher Kim. Everyone clapped. "Thank you for the quiz, Teacher Kim," said Mia. "It was a good game." "Next Thursday, I want a harder quiz," said Leo. Teacher Kim smiled. "Then you can make the cards," she said.
